name: Cyxtera (Digital Realty Trust) Citibank Data Center

profile.address: 1919, Park Avenue, The Shades, Weehawken, Hudson County, New Jersey, 07086
profile.reading: This record is named Cyxtera (Digital Realty Trust) Citibank Data Center in this registry, mapped to Weehawken, New Jersey, a name that already associates this facility with Digital Realty Trust and with a Citibank tenant relationship in the registry own pre-existing data. No corporate website could be reached for this operator this session, and no independent secondary source was found this session to confirm or contradict that existing name, so it is carried forward unchanged as existing registry data rather than independently verified this session, and address, capacity, and square footage remain not published in this record. Cyxtera Technologies, headquartered in Coral Gables, Florida, entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement with Brookfield Infrastructure, disclosed via an SEC Form 8-K titled "Cyxtera x Brookfield APA Press Release" and filed November 2, 2023, per SEC EDGAR's full-text search index; this registry has not independently confirmed the full scope of that transaction (whether it covered Cyxtera's entire US colocation portfolio or a subset), nor whether it touches this specific Weehawken facility or its pre-existing Digital Realty and Citibank associations. Separately, Cologix, a different operator tracked elsewhere in this registry, acquired two specific Cyxtera facilities, VAN5 in Vancouver and MTL12 in Montreal, in 2023, per Cologix's own materials; those two Canadian facilities are unrelated to this New Jersey facility and to the Brookfield transaction. Cyxtera's own public website resolves but displays content that reads as dated (referencing a 2017 executive appointment) with no current facility locations list, and its data-centers subpage returns a certificate error, a combination consistent with a company mid-transition following the Brookfield transaction rather than one actively maintaining public marketing infrastructure. No square footage, MW capacity, or current operational status specific to this Weehawken facility was located in sourcing reachable this session. Fresh research this session, using web search tools unavailable in the prior exhausted pass, identifies Cyxteras Weehawken campus, known as NJ2 or EWR2, at 300 Boulevard East, a four story building with a 12 inch raised floor and a stated PUE of 1.75, though this entry cannot confirm this rows own reverse geocoded Park Avenue coordinates correspond precisely to that building rather than a nearby address in the same Shades neighborhood, and does not assign building specific figures on that basis. Baxtel reports the site was acquired as part of the 2.8 billion dollar, 57 data center CenturyLink portfolio deal that closed in May 2017 and formed Cyxtera Technologies. Cyxtera itself filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2023; Brookfield Infrastructure Partners agreed to acquire seven of Cyxteras US data centers for 775 million dollars in a deal that closed in early 2024, merging retained Cyxtera facilities with Brookfields Evoque colocation platform into a combined operator later rebranded Centersquare in April 2024.

reading.body:
The Weehawken campus, now operated as Centersquare following a 2024 rebranding of merged Cyxtera and Evoque platforms, sits in a narrow slice of New Jersey's mapped data center footprint. Of 48 facilities mapped in the state, only 5 publish power specifications; this site ranks sixth by published megawatts, though the operator reports separate utility (45.7 MW) and UPS (20.7 MW) figures without clarifying which represents IT-critical load, so the true available capacity for compute remains opaque. The facility holds 199,110 square feet of raised floor across four stories at a stated PUE of 1.75, with 31 MW of standby generation capacity.

Translating the published utility supply to rack density requires an assumption: at 40 kW per rack as a common colocation standard, 45.7 MW utility supply spans roughly 1,140 racks, though this figure does not account for overhead, resilience hardware, or the split between IT and facility loads that the separate UPS figure hints at. Higher-density AI training setups would compress this estimate; the actual AI-ready rack count depends on the mix of tenants and workloads the operator accepts. The campus holds SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications, qualifying it for regulated workloads and high-assurance deployments.

Weehawken's rank within New Jersey's published capacity reflects both its actual size and the state's sparse publication of power figures; no independent verification of the utility or UPS claims is published in this record. The facility's ownership chain—formed in CenturyLink's 2017 portfolio sale to Cyxtera, surviving Cyxtera's 2023 bankruptcy, and merged into Centersquare in early 2024—carries operational risk and uncertainty typical of assets caught in major restructuring. Whether this campus will scale or remain a legacy colocation platform is not answered by the published data.
